Robot Framework gives every run a set of **built-in variables** — automatic
values you can read without declaring them: `${TEST_NAME}`, `${CURDIR}` (the
suite's folder), `${OUTPUT_DIR}`, and more.

Variables also have **scope** and **priority**. A `VAR` can be local (default),
`TEST`, `SUITE`, or `GLOBAL`. And a value set on the command line with
`--variable NAME:value` **overrides** the `*** Variables ***` section, so you
can retarget a run without editing files.

```diagram
stack "VAR scope: how far a value reaches"
GLOBAL -- the whole run, every suite
SUITE -- this suite and its tests
TEST -- this test only
local -- default: one keyword or block
note "CLI --variable NAME:value overrides the *** Variables *** section"
```

## Task 1 — Use a built-in variable and a scoped VAR

**Goal:** create `checks/scopes.robot` with a test that reads a built-in
variable, and another that creates a `SUITE`-scoped variable with `VAR`.

Here is the same idea with different built-ins and a different value. Adapt them.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Reads Built In Values
    Should Not Be Empty    ${SUITE_NAME}
    Log    Output goes to ${OUTPUT_DIR}

Var With Scope
    VAR    ${token}    abc123    scope=SUITE
    Should Be Equal    ${token}    abc123
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `checks/scopes.robot` defines the test `Built In Variables Exist`,
and it passes.

<!-- hint -->
Read a built-in without declaring it: `Should Not Be Empty    ${TEST_NAME}` and
`Log    Running from ${CURDIR}`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Create a scoped variable with `VAR    ${shared}    hello    scope=SUITE`, then
assert it equals `hello`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Built In Variables Exist
    Should Not Be Empty    ${TEST_NAME}
    Log    Running from ${CURDIR}

Scoped Var Is Set
    VAR    ${shared}    hello    scope=SUITE
    Should Be Equal    ${shared}    hello
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run the suite green

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the test `Built In Variables Exist` passes.
